item.title: Katherine Town Council removes CEO Ingrid Stonhill without explanation
item.description: Katherine Town Council has removed chief executive officer Ingrid Stonhill without explanation following more than four months of unexplained leave, a move which comes months after the council was ordered by the Fair Work Commission to pay staff performance wage increases they had been denied by Ms Stonhill since July 2022.

item.title: Opinion: Governance reform at CDU is long overdue
item.description: OPINION: The Charles Darwin University governing Council lacks the competency to govern and manage the institution, thereby undermining the NT's higher education sector and the economy, writes Dr Don Fuller.

item.title: Another Labor govt investment goes under with taxpayers on the hook – but no inquiry needed, Chief Minister says
item.description: A rocket launching company the previous Labor government invested more than $5 million of public funds into has gone into liquidation, with the Chief Minister mocking Labor again for their poor investment decisions, but refusing to answer questions about whether she would now call a public inquiry into how Labor wasted millions of taxpayer money investing in doomed private business enterprises.

item.title: NT Criminal Court list – with charges – Mar 10
item.description: The 216 names facing criminal courts in the Northern Territory for Tuesday, March 10, 2026. This list includes all the charges.

item.title: Humpty Doo man charged with producing child abuse material
item.description: A 42-year-old Humpty Doo man was apprehended at a Palmerston shopping centre Sunday morning by the joint anti-child exploitation team and later charged with producing and transmitting child abuse material, NT Police said.

item.title: CLP MLA accused of bullying female staffers says he is ‘considering legal options’ but offers no explanation
item.description: CLP backbencher Tanzil Rahman broke weeks of silence Sunday over bullying allegations in an unusual statement from his electorate office rather than through the CLP's highly-paid spin doctors, stating he was "deeply offended" by the allegations and "actively considering my legal options".

item.title: Labor likely to win Nightcliff with assist from CLP, disinterest from voters
item.description: A Labor candidate who sought endorsements from reviled former chief ministers Michael Gunner and Natasha Fyles appears likely to win the Nightcliff by-election with help from the CLP after preferences, according to updated figures on Monday afternoon.

item.title: Firearm charges after man at casino later arrested with gun in car: Police
item.description: UPDATED: An allegedly intoxicated man who reportedly attempted to assault people as he left the Mindil Beach Casino early Monday morning was later arrested in Durack after an officer found an unregistered gun in his car, NT Police said, later clarifying the firearm is an air gun and not a Glock as it was originally called in the supplied picture.

item.title: Investigation into Katherine Town Council kept secret
item.description: The Local Government Minister and the Katherine Town Council will not say why an investigation was launched into the council last year, but the NT Independent understands it probed elected members' understanding of their roles and the now former chief executive's performance.

item.title: ‘Unprecedented situation’: Boil water alert now issued after Darwin River Dam pump station fails
item.description: UPDATED: NT Health has issued a boil water alert for Darwin and Palmerston after Power and Water asked residents to immediately reduce their water usage following the Darwin River Dam pump station shutting down around 4:30pm Monday due to ongoing heavy rains in the region and flash flooding, in what the operator has labelled an "unprecedented situation" which could take up to two days to get back on line.
